Commentary.Commentary: Right then! England would require a terrific batting effort from their senior men if they are to stand a chance. If their first innings is anything to look by, then it wouldn't be wrong to predict that this can be over soon. Will they come out fighting or will the hosts' bowlers run through that batting line-up? We shall find out once the second session gets underway...

Australia will not be too happy with their own batting performance. True, the pitch is not the easiest to bat on but this certainly does not look like one where the scorecard shows the highest score as 20. They will hope that the target of 354 proves enough.

Chris Woakes, too continued from where he left off last evening and picked up 4 to his name. Now that, they have done the job with the ball they still have their task cut out. The writing seems to be on the wall for them.

So, England have bundled out the Aussies here in the first session but tell you what, the hosts are still right on top as they have a big lead in their kitty. Reducing the opposition to 4/53 overnight, England stepped in with a lot of confidence this morning. Anderson and Broad bowled tight lines and didn't leak too many. Eventually, it was the former who got his side the first breakthrough. The highlight of the session was him bagging his first Test 5-fer in Australia and also taking 800 international wickets.

OUT! AUSTRALIA HAVE BEEN BOWLED OUT FOR 138, LEAD BY 353! Overton from around the wicket, bangs in a short ball on the body. Hazlewood was never comfortable in playing that one. Doesn't know how to counter this as he just hangs his bat out taking his eyes off the ball. The ball takes the edge and flies towards Malan at gully who takes a diving catch forward.
Shortish and angling in on the body, Cummins backs away and awkwardly punches it through the cover region for a single.
Shortish again on the body, Cummins plays it towards point off the back foot.
Fuller in length, Josh leans a bit and drives it through mid off. He wanted the second and Woakes offers a helping hand by slowly running behind the ball but Australia are happy with one.
Goes around the wicket and bowls a bumper on middle. Hazlewood ducks late but in the end manages to evade it.
Starts off with a short of a length delivery outside off, Cummins backs away and hits it to deep point for a single.
Craig Overton is brought into the attack. He bowled just 1 over last evening.
On the pads, clipped around the corner for a single. THE LEAD TOUCHES 350 NOW!
Pushes it through covers and takes one.
Stands back to this length delivery and offers a straight bat.
Bouncer! The batsman does well to evade it.
Opens the bat face and glides it through backward point for a single.
Another short ball on middle by Anderson, Cummins sits under it.
Shortish and just outside off, it skids off the deck, Cummins arches back to play but gets a top edge which flies down to third man. Three runs taken.
The batsman tries hooking that one but misses it completely.
The short of length delivery has been cut away through square on the off side.
Clips it towards the vacant mid-wicket region but Woakes is quick to run and deny the single on offer.
Swing and a miss! Angles it away from a length on middle, Cummins wildly swings across the line. Gets beaten.
Some changes in the field. There is third man, deep point and two gullies.
Nicely played! Short and climbing in on Hazlewood who stands and steers it through backward point. Runs the first one hard but doesn't take another.
Bangs in a short delivery again, Cummins once again ducks. A good over from Anderson!
Goes fuller after a couple of short ball, Pat works it towards the leg side.
Another bouncer, but dealt with ease this time.
Anderson now has his tail up. Hits the deck hard, surprised the batsman with the bounce who somehow manages to duck under it.
Josh Hazlewood is the last man in! How long can he last?

OUT! Anderson gets a 5-fer, his first one in Australia. He has been made to work hard for this and he can finally sink in the moment. Well done, Jimmy! The whole of Adelaide Oval applauds the effort as he shows the cherry around the ground. That's the most wonderful feeling ever. Ball - Fuller in length and around off, Starc tries to go big down the ground. Miscues it high in the air and it's a simple catch to Moeen Ali at mid off who moves swiftly to his right and takes it with ease. Australia lead by 343 runs!
Fuller in length and angling in on the pads, flicked through square leg for a couple.
Brave lad! He is back on the ground. Anderson wants that 5-fer.
Looks to poke at the delivery outside off, gets beaten all ends up.
Fuller and wider outside off, Cummins lets it be.
Bangs in a short ball, pat ducks.
Wide outside off stump, the batsman leaves it alone.
Good length on the stumps, defended down.
Fuller on off, driven straight to cover.

Chance! A catch and then even a run out. Anderson nearly picks up a 5-fer here! But he is down in agony. He has hurt his right knee. I will tell you how! Anderson bowls a short ball on middle, Starc looks to tuck it away but gets a leading edge as the ball lobs straight up in the air. Jimmy runs to take it, gets to the ball but with the momentum he slides, drags his right knee and disturbs the stumps at the striker's end. In doing all this, the ball pops out of his hands. Starc was out of the crease so even if the ball after popping out of the hands had hit the stumps, the Aussie pacer would have been run out.
Is Anderson in trouble? He has dragged his right knee on the ground while taking a catch. He ripped his trouser in doing so. He is walking off the field. Not good for England.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
This one cuts back in, leaves the batsman alone. The ball goes past the inside edge en route the keeper.
Back of a length delivery outside off, Cummins punches it through covers. Gets it through the gap and takes three.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Fuller in length and outside off, left alone.
James Anderson comes back. He is on the road to pick up his 1st ever 5-fer in this part of the world. Can he?
Back of a length delivery on middle, tucked behind square on the leg side for a single.
Short of a length delivery, rises off the deck. Cummins though takes his eyes off the ball but manages to fend it away. There is no short leg, which means the ball dies down safely.
Back of a length outside off, Cummins pushes it towards point off the back foot.
Shortish on the stumps, Cummins hops a bit and defends.
Pat Cummins is the next man in, replacing Marsh. He took 37 balls to get off the mark in the first innings. Shouldn't be the case this time.

OUT! Chris Woakes has a 4-fer now! Shaun Marsh is finally being dismissed in this Test. Fuller in length, curling back in a bit, Marsh was eyeing that wide mid on area as he looks to work it away. But there is a bit of inward movement which takes the inside edge and cannons onto the stumps. He walks back but Australia have a lead of 337!
Length delivery, just around middle and off, Marsh stays back in defense.
The batsman has punched the ball off the back foot.

SIX! When Starc hits it, it stays hit! Such is the power of this man! Ali bowls it full and in the slot for Starc who gets down and pummels it over deep mid-wicket for a maximum. Runs have started to flow now for the hosts.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Punches it off the back foot through covers for a single.

Was there an edge? But what bounce for Ali! Lyon will be surely watching this! Flatter and rising from a length, Marsh goes back to cut but gets beaten by the bounce. Bairstow fumbles and eventually puts it down. Snicko shows there was no edge though.

FOUR! Excellent! Marsh was trying to do this since the last over of Ali but mid off was there to cut it off! This time he gets what he wants! Loopy delivery outside off, Marsh dances down the track and drives it off the meat through covers for a boundary.

FOUR! Edgy... Australia wouldn't mind but England would! Angles it away on a length outside off, Starc swings at it. Gets a thick edge which flies safely through gully and backward point for a streaky boundary to end the over. Australia's total reaches Nelson!
Good bounce for Woakes! Bends his back, gets that extra bounce which he is looking for. Starc nearly falls for it. Tries to fend it awkwardly but the ball goes just past the gloves to the keeper.
Fuller in length and curling back in a bit, Marsh drives it off the inner  half towards mid on for a single.
Fuller in length and outside off, Marsh leans forward and strokes it straight to the man at mid off.
Goes fuller, keeps the line outside off, Marsh blocks it out gently.
Slants it away on a length, just outside the off stump line. Marsh ain't playing at that.
Good running! Moeen Ali once again lands it around off, Marsh comes down the track to drive but gets it off the edge. Rolls past first slip and Starc calls him through for a brisk single.
Around middle and leg, bunted back down the ground to the bowler.
Drifting in and then turning away but the length is full which allows Marsh to cover the line and keep it out.
Replica of the last ball. Can't beat the man at mid off again.
Tossed up outside off, a gentle push but straight to mid off.
Comes out of the crease and blocks it down.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Hits the deck hard, Starc watches it early. Carefully lets it sail over to Jonny.
Length delivery around middle and leg, Mitchell looks to tuck it away but is early into the shot. Misses and wears it on the pads.

A run out chance! But no damage done! Woakes bowls a length delivery on middle, Starc stands tall and just lifts it down the ground. Broad from mid off gets to the ball. Now, Starc wants the third which was on but Shaun Marsh isn't too keen to run. Sends Starc back who is more than halfway down the track. The throw comes in towards Woakes and there is a run out opportunity at the striker's end but the bowler fumbles. Starc, meanwhile dives to get back in.
Length outside off, played towards point.
Outside off, Starc doesn't play at it.

SHAUN IS SAFE! As expected! Mooen Ali drifts it into the batsman, Marsh lunges forward to defend but the ball turns away a bit and goes past the outside edge. He loses his balance as Bairstow behind the stumps takes the bails off. He doesn't appeal but someone from his team does. It's taken upstairs. Replays show, Marsh has his foot grounded.
There is a stumping appeal against Shaun Marsh. Bairstow though didn't appeal but not sure who did. Marsh looks confident.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Moeen Ali just can't bowl it down leg. Too easy for Shaun who clips it through backward square leg for a couple.
Flattish through the air around middle and off, defended from within the crease.
Fuller around middle and leg, defended off the front foot.

Drifting in around the leg stump, Starc just tickles it away fine. Bairstow gives a long chase. By the time he gets to the ball, they take three. England will now have to chase a reocrd total at this venue, if they are to win.
Is happy to stays in the crease and offer a straight bat.

FOUR! Edged and that goes over the slip cordon! Woakes slants it away on a length outside off, gives width and the southpaw decides to go after it. Flashes hard at it and gets a thick edge which flies over the slip cordon for a boundary.
Gets right behind the line and stabs it out towards the cover fielder.

This is a nervy shot from Starc! Sees the full length delivery and decides to go big. Gets a leading edge which lobs up in the air on the off side. Luckily for him it flies way over the man at extra cover. Only a single results.
Back of a length and a bit wide outside off, defended awkwardly off the back foot towards cover.
Length delivery outside off, Marsh taps it in front of point and calls through for a quick single.
Goes back and punches it towards the cover fielder for nothing. Another good over from Moeen. A maiden!
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.

Darts it around middle and leg, not a good option as Starc can sweep it away as there is no man at fine leg. This time he looks to push it back down the track, gets an inside edge on the pads as the ball rolls towards Moeen.
Short mid-wicket goes to backward point. Two slips in place too...
Edgyy! Lands it around middle, gets it to turn away a touch, Starc goes back to work it away but gets it off the edge past first slip. Two runs picked up.
A bit flatter through the air around middle, Starc stays back to keep it out.
Floats it up around middle, defended by lunging forward.
Angles it away from a length around middle, Marsh lifts his bat to make a leave. A successful over from Woakes.
Shortish and around middle and off, defended with a straight bat.
Mitchell Starc walks out next to bat, replacing Paine.

OUT! Tim Paine departs! But this is another excellent catch from England. We saw Malan taking one a while back and now it's Overton! Woakes bangs in a short ball outside off, it hurries onto the batsman who tries to pull. Gets a top edge that lobs high up in the air. The man from square leg runs backward and Overton from deep backward square leg runs forward. Ideally, the latter is in the position to take it. He runs in and puts a dive forward. Then stretches both his hands and takes it beautifully. Maybe, it was due to the wind why he had to dive. Nevertheless, Australia lead by 305 runs!
Fuller in length and on the stumps, Tim pushes it back to the bowler who collects and mimes a throw back at the stumps.
Fuller and angling in, worked straight to the man at short mid-wicket.
Shortish and angling in, Tim Paine stays behind the line to keep it out.

Almost! Shaun Marsh tries to use his feet which is a good thing. But Ali spots that and fires it full on the stumps. The southpaw tries to jam it out but gets an inside edge on the pads as the ball rolls towards the off side. Just a single from the over.
Marsh leans forward and defends it into the ground.
Fuller around off, driven through covers for a single.
Good stop from Woakes! Saved a certain boundary! Short and outside off, Paine camps back and cuts. Chris at backward point dives full length to his left to make a good stop.
A bit flat and short outside off, punched off the back foot towards the cover fielder.
Starts off with a loopy ball around off, Paine lunges forward and pushes it towards cover. Wants a single but Ali himself runs to the ball to deny them.

DRINKS are on the field. England's period of play. They have been incisive and been purposeful. Not too many wasteful deliveries and the result of that has been 2 wickets within the first 30 minutes. However, the lead will now start to play on their minds. Already Australia are 304 ahead and another 45 runs could put the game beyond England's reach. Also, the next challenge for England would be the other bowlers now stepping up after the initial bursts by Anderson and Broad. Here is spin for the first time today. MOEEN ALI to bowl.
Perhaps the first full ball of this over, driven straight to mid off.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot.
Full and outside off, driven towards cover.
A length ball outside off, Marsh feels for the ball but then it cuts back in. Beats the inside edge and just misses the off stump!
Outside off, left alone.
A short ball outside off, watchfully defended.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
On middle, flicked to the leg side for a single.
The batsman plays it with an angled bat and guides it to gully.
Full and outside off, defended to the off side.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
On a length around middle and leg, played towards square leg.
Outside off, left alone.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot.

OVERTHROWS! FOUR! Oh dear... poor stuff from Stuart Broad. Paine pushes it towards point and calls for a single. Marsh responds but then is sent back. Shaun is in no man's land, has to stop, then turn. But he slips a touch. However, he manages to turn around in time and dives in his crease. James Vince comes running in from backward point, gets to the ball and has a shy at the bowler's end. Misses but would not have mattered even if he had hit. But hello, what is Broad doing there? He is in line to stop the throw but the ball goes right beneath his hands to the boundary behind! THE AUSSIE LEAD CROSSES 300 and Michael Vaughan on air feels this is enough. But somewhere, deep down in his heart, he feels that England can chase it down.

On a length outside off, Tim comes forward and looks to tap. Gets a bit of an outside edge which goes on the ground through the slip cordon but Dawid Malan dives to his left and stops it. That was a boundary.
Landed outside off, Paine feels for it but misses.
A length ball on middle and leg, tucked through square leg for a single.
Chris Woakes into the attack. He was excellent as well last evening.
Too straight, clipped through mid-wicket for a couple.
Outside off, left alone.
Outside off, Paine feels for the ball outside off and is beaten.
Full and outside off, Paine comes forward, tries to push it away but gets squared up a touch. The result is an outside edge but it does not carry to second slip as he played that with soft hands.
Landed outside off, defended from the crease.
Full and outside off, pushed towards cover.
Outside off, left alone.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Full again, Shaun gets right behind the line of the ball and defends.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Full and outside off, left alone.
On a good length outside off, defended from the crease.

Full and outside off, driven down the ground. He calls through for the quick single and substitute Tom Curran gets to the ball. He aims a shy at the bowler's end but misses. Marsh would have been in though. There was a chance for an overthrow but square leg dived to his left to stop that.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Outside off, left alone.

Full and outside off, Paine comes forward gets to the pitch of the ball and drives it through the covers. The batsmen take the second, Paine hesitates for the third but Marsh calls him through. Here is the basic difference between Paine and Handscomb. The latter plays back to full deliveries while the former's first approach is to come forward.
Outside off, left alone this time.
Landed outside off, Paine plays inside the line and is beaten.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Full and outside off, Paine just works it through mid-wicket and gets off the mark with a single. Just a tap and run.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Full on middle, swinging in prodigiously, Marsh watches it closely and then flicks it towards fine leg for a single.
Outside off, left alone.
Full and outside off, Marsh defends watchfully.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through. Excellent over from Jimmy. He has now got a 4-fer.
Full and outside off, Paine shoulders arms.

Tim Paine walks in at number 8, replacing Handscomb. Paine's initial counter-attack in the first innings put England off. If he can do something similar here, his team can get to a position from where they cannot lose.

OUT! Straight to the man! Catching practice but make no mistake, it is a good take. Landed outside off, between full and good, Handscomb backs away a touch and guides it towards third man. But he does not find the gap, nor does he try to keep the ball down. It goes thick and fast but straight to Dawid Malan at gully who does well to take it low to his right. If you have ever observed coaches giving catching practice behind the wicket before the start of play, Handscomb can give a good audition. End of a struggle for Peter. He never looked comfortable out there. Neither today, nor in the first innings, nor in the first Test. Axe on the head beckoning perhaps... Meanwhile, ANDERSON HAS PICKED UP HIS 50TH TEST WICKET IN AUSTRALIA. Yet to take a fifer though. Can he do it today?
Outside off, Handscomb feels for it but misses.
The batsman has punched the ball off the back foot.
Full and outside off, pushed straight to cover.
WIDE. That is a surprising call. A short ball yes, but it was not that high. Handscomb ducks.
Landed outside off, left alone.
Played to the mid-wicket region by the batsman.
A length ball outside off, Shaun gets across, feels for it but misses.
Outside off, Marsh gets across and shoulders arms.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
Full and outside off, driven straight to mid off.
Full and outside off, PH gets across to flick but misses by a long way.
Lucky again. Full outside off, Peter gets across and looks to flick but gets a leading edge through cover. Two runs taken.
A short ball now, Handscomb gets out of the line of the delivery.
Poor. New man in, but the ball is on leg stump. Easy tuck through square leg for a single to get off the mark.
Shaun Marsh walks in at number 7, replacing Lyon. Australia need their first innings hero to stand up again.

OUT! Caught! England get rid of the nightwatchman eventually. That hit on the helmet seemed to have stirred him. A length ball outside off, Lyon backs away and just attempts a slash over the off side. But he can only get it as far as mid off where Broad completes the formalities. A handy 14 from Lyon which is what Warner managed as well, in this innings and it is more than what his skipper could muster. Australia are effectively 286/5.

Fine shot. A length ball outside off, Handscomb punches it past the diving man at short extra cover. Broad chases it from mid off and slides near the boundary to save a run for his side. Just one question - what is Broad doing at mid off? He just finished a fine over. He should be either at fine leg or some other place where he does not have to do any running.
Lucky! A length ball, outside off, Lyon looks to heave it to the on side but gets a leading edge. Anderson runs to his left from mid off but cannot get there! Two runs taken.
Full and outside off, NH looks to drive but misses.

Root now comes and has a word with his bowler. He might have been asking about an extra man on the off side but Broad says no. He seems to indicate that the ball was not bad but the batsman backed away. No field changes.
FOUR! A tail-ender's square drive, says Warne on air! A length ball in line of the stumps, Lyon backs away and just steers it behind point for a boundary!
Another bouncer, Nathan ducks this time.
FOUR! Terrific response! A short ball outside off but Lyon is ready. He waits for the ball and ramps it over the slips to third man!
Short leg comes in now. Double bluff or a short ball coming?

The physio is out in the middle. It seems more of a breather for Lyon. He is just being talked into, just to make sure that there is no concussion or a headache. No tablets, nothing. Just talking. Now, the replacement comes in for the helmet.

ON THE HELMET! Lyon is okay. Nothing dangerous. Just seems to be a bit shaken. A short ball right at the body, Lyon takes his eyes off the ball and sways away at the last moment. Is hit flush on the grill. Broad straightaway walks over to him and has a chat, to check whether he is okay. Hang on... Lyon did not realize one thing. The back flap of the helmet was falling down and was not far from the stumps.
He gets one away! Looks like Handscomb just heard Warne on air. Gets across his stumps and does he what likes to best. Flicks it through mid-wicket for a couple.

Shane Warne is not quite happy with the negativity shown on the field here. First, he says that England are wasting the morning conditions here by not consistently bowling in the right areas. They are not making the batsmen play every ball. Then, he is not happy with Peter Handscomb as he is just looking to survive, not even rotating the strike. What that will do is, play right into England's hands as even though wickets won't come, Australia won't be going anywhere. Then, he goes a step further and analyzes. If the Aussies score 40-50 runs and set England a target in excess of 300, Warne is not confident the visitors can chase it down. Gosh. Eventually, he says that Handscomb just needs to get a little bit busier and try and rotate the strike.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Back of a length outside off, Peter defends it from his crease.
Outside off, a play and a miss.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Full and outside off, watchfully defended.
Full on middle, pushed straight to mid on.
Square leg drops back. Short ball coming? He was trying to hook almost every ball in the first innings.

No luck for Broad. He is starting to find his length. It needs to be between that full and good. Not too full, not good, not length not anything. That in-between one. The line has to be just outside off. Lyon looks to drive but misses.
Full and straight, Nathan shows a good compact defense as he pushes the ball to mid on.
Outside off, left alone.
There is that line... full and outside off, a tempter, drive me if you can, Lyon accepts the challenge but comes second best. Luckily for the batsman, he does not edge it.
On a length around off, watchfully defended.
Around off, watchfully defended.
The batsman works it down the leg side.
Full and outside off, driven through the covers. The fielder dives to his right but gets only a hand to it. By the time Stuart Broad can get to the ball from mid off, two runs are taken.
Back of an length outside off, Handscomb defends it from his crease.
The batsman fails to put bat on ball.
A length ball on middle, flicked straight to square leg.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Full and outside off, driven straight to mid off.
Another short ball outside off, Lyon sways away. That is a waste of a delivery.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Full on middle, pushed straight to mid on.
Landed outside off, short in length, left alone.
Stuart Broad to bowl from the other end.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Excellent bowling. Variation of length. It is much fuller, PH thinks he can flick but gets a leading edge to cover.
Again, extra bounce, Peter feels for it and fends it towards gully.

NOT OUT! Decision overturned! No bat involved. But a terrific delivery first up. A short ball right at the body of the batsman, Handscomb comes first but then the ball shoots up suddenly. He is taken by surprise and does not have enough time to play that. Tries to fend that and ends up nicking it to first slip. That is what we all felt. So did England. Cook took the catch and appealed but there was no reaction from Aleem Dar. Then, after a long pause, he raised his finger. Handscomb immediately reviewed and Snikcometer showed a spike when the ball went past the bat. Then another spike when the ball was nowhere near the bat. Understandably, the third umpire said he is not sure. He now got the Hot Spot and luckily for Handscomb, there is nothing on it. The ball actually had hit the shoulder. Handscomb is lucky there. There was a delay in Hot Spot generation. Had that not come, given that the third umpire was not sure, the decision would have stayed.
EDGED AND TAKEN! Handscomb has been caught behind! But he has reviewed it...
A short ball outside off, Handscomb keeps his bat inside the line.
Lyon is away. A length ball down the leg side, Lyon tucks it through square leg for a single.

It is bright and sunny and the players are out in the middle. England's first aim would be to dislodge the nightwatchman Nathan Lyon as quickly as possible. Here is Jimmy Anderson to Nathan Lyon first up. Here we go...

What we witnessed in that final hour on Monday was perhaps the best bowling display by England in this series. Anderson and Broad made the ball dance and then Woakes did not let the pressure drop down. Criticism, if any, could be the fact that they wasted the new ball but have more than made up for it.

13 wickets fell on what is called the moving day of a Test match. Australia did a decent job in taking 9 wickets of England but then themselves lost 4 wickets to keep parity in the game. They still lead by 268 and would need at least another 100 runs to stay ahead. Can England keep them below that?
... DAY 4, SESSION 1 ...

The Aussies lead by 268, and the odds are still stacked in their favour. But if England can produce something similar tomorrow and wrap the hosts up quickly in the morning session, then we have a serious game on our hands. The experienced campaigners in the English side will need to raise their hand up and stand to be counted. Day 4 is going to bring unadulterated joy to all the cricketing fans across the globe. You don't want to miss this. Join in for all the action. See you then, Munchkins!

What a wonderful day of Test match cricket. You couldn't be expecting anything more. Had everything in it to keep it lively and electric. Pure pandemonium! After bowling England out for 227 and gaining a healthy lead of 215, the last session was going to be a difficult one to bat in. With the lights and the new ball coming into play, Australia would have had to be on top of their game to weather the storm, but England, in particular Jimmy Anderson, came out pumping battery acid in their veins. Bowled a long spell, one north of 10 overs and it reaped dividends as he picked up two wickets. Chris Woakes stepped his game up and scalped the two big guns in Warner and Smith.

What a juicy delivery to end the day. Perfect. Total excitement here. Woakes with a length delivery on middle and off, it straightens up after angling in and takes the leading edge of Nathan Lyon's bat. Goes square through point and a single is taken. That's it, was the last over of the day. STUMPS ON DAY 3!
Fuller length delivery outside off, Nathan Lyon offers no stroke to that one.

The physio is out to have a look at Nathan Lyon. He got hit on the high pad, started rubbing it and stretching it afterwards. Jonny Bairstow is laughing at this sight, he knows why he's doing it, the Adelaide Oval knows why he's doing it. It's going to happen either way, the ticking of the clock never stops. The physio is out, even he can't control his laughter. He whips out the magic spray though, applies some and then goes back.
Back of a length delivery cutting back in sharply, raps Lyon high on the thigh pad who misses his defensive shot. He appears to be in some kind of pain, walks away from the crease rubbing his thigh.

What are you doing there, Nate? Such a dangerous shot to play at this stage. It's wide outside off, Lyon walks across and goes for the cover drive. The away swing takes the ball past the outside edge and into the keeper's gloves. Steady now, king of the jungle. You're almost home. No need to do this.
Fullish in length and close to the off stump, Lyon brings down a straight blade in defense.
Angling in, then moving away off the seam, Nathan Lyon has nothing to do with that one.
Beaten! Peach from the big pacer! In the corridor of uncertainty, Handscomb hangs his blade and is beaten past the outside edge.
Length delivery from Broad, nice and straight, Handscomb catches the edge but to his credit, he plays with soft hands and the ball falls short of the slip cordon.
Watchful from Handscomb. Keeps his eyes on the ball till the last second, ducks and lets it be.

What are you doing there? So risky, needs to be more careful. Fuller outside off, Handscomb attempts to leave it late, a little too late really, as the ball goes off the bottom half of the bat behind to the slip cordon.
Good length ball in the channel outside off, tapped gently on the off side from within the crease.
Seeing the ball pitching comfortably outside off, Peter Handscomb decides to leave it alone.
Short of a good length on the fifth stump line, kept out well to end the over.
Beaten! Woakes brings it closer to the off stick, keeps it on a length as Nathan Lyon tries to defend. Past the outside edge and into the keeper's gloves.
Well outside after landing on a good length, left alone for the keeper to collect.

Edged and through! Length delivery angling away from around off, Lyon edges and it goes right through the slip cordon, after falling short of them to begin with. Two runs taken. Woakes isn't happy, he wanted that to be stopped.
The nightwatchman Nathan Lyon is out to bat.

OUT! CHRIS WOAKES HAS GOT STEVEN SMITH! This could be the defining moment in this game. The big fish is hunted and England are elated here. Woakes with an absolute beauty as he lands it on a length around off, it angles in and beats Smith's defense. Catches him on the back pad and there's a loud shout. The umpire is convinced, he signals out but Steven Smith will not give in. He reviews. Takes it upstairs and replays show that the impact is umpire's call and it's even clipping the stumps, which is also the umpire's call. So the Australian skipper is gone and this is a huge moment for the Englishmen. The lead is 265.
Review! Steven Smith the man in the limelight again. A decision for an lbw against him is in question.
Hits the deck hard as Woakes pounds it on a shorter length, Smith rises and keeps it down.
Full delivery on off, driven to mid off.
Well away from the off stump, the batsman remains confident he doesn't want to play at that.
Short of a good length in the off stump channel, blocked out solidly off the back foot.
Shortish in length outside off, moves away off the surface as Handscomb hangs his bat out to it. Goes past the edge and Bairstow dives low to his right to collect it.
Handscomb is watchful as this is landed on a length outside off. It comes back in but he has his line covered well to avoid any kind of danger.
Zips off the deck as it lands on a length outside off, Peter with a good leave.
Stuart Broad is back into the bowling attack. Anderson's done his part, can the big man send one of the two batsmen out there back to the dressing room?
Good pace and decent carry for Anderson, outside off, Smith rather stylishly shoulders his arms and leaves it alone.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
That's a lovely shot. Handscomb offers a firm punch through the gap in the covers and runs hard to come back for the third. The 50 comes up for Australia with that.
Angling in at first and then straightening up from around off, Peter Handscomb covers the line and taps it down on the off side.
Touch fuller, around off, guarded out from the front foot on the off side.
On a good length and outside the line of off stump, Handscomb covers his off stick and lets it be.
Over the wicket for the final ball of the over, strays this on the pads, Smith clips it through towards deep square leg and takes two.

It's all happening here in Adelaide! James Anderson is breathing fire in this evening session. Lands it outside leg and it swings back towards off to ping Steven Smith on the back pad as he attempts to flick. He'd have wished that ball pitched in line, total ripper!

FOUR! The class of this player! Packed on side field but it doesn't matter one bit to him. Flicks this full ball through the gap, between mid-wicket and square leg and finds the fence. Terrific execution of the shot.
Full in length, attacking the stumps, Smith is half-forward and defends it out.
Outside off on a good length, Smith covers the line and lets it be.

NOT OUT! A REVERSAL! No inside edge after all, it's pitched outside leg. Oh my good lord, how close was that? Jimmy Anderson comes from around the wicket to Steven Smith and bowls it fuller, catches him on the pads right in front of the stumps and there's a big appeal. The umpire raises his finger, Smith ponders whether to take the DRS, and eventually he does after speaking to Handscomb. It's taken upstairs and much to Anderson and England's dismay, the ball has pitched outside the line of leg stump. Anything else beyond that is irrelevant now. The Australian skipper carries on, the Adelaide Oval breathes a huge sigh of relief.
Big moment in the game! Steven Smith has been adjudged lbw. But... But... Could there be an inside edge? Going to be close. Over to the third umpire now.
Ooooohhhh... That was close. Woakes spears it full outside off, Handscomb brings his bat down, gets an edge, but the ball goes behind to the slip cordon on the bump.
Peter Handscomb will be next in to bat. Two slips and a gully in place.

OUT! DAVID WARNER IS GONE! This is the wicket England wanted. That's a big one, really big one. The dangerous Warner departs. Woakes gets his line right and keeps it around off. It's angling away late and squares up David a touch. The edge is drawn and Joe Root at second slip takes a wonderful catch. Can another wicket be had here for the Englishmen? They have their tails up, have every chance to do so.
Nicely done. The ball is quite full, but David Warner is up for this. He gets right behind the line of the ball and blocks it out.
Too full and too straight from Chris Woakes, flicked through mid-wicket for a brace.
Angling across yet again, another leave by the southpaw.
Slanting across on a good length, David Warner watches the ball as it goes through to the keeper.
Full and swinging in, Smith defends it off the inner half on the leg side. That'll be the end of the over.
Interesting. Stays around the wicket to Steven Smith and bowls a length ball on middle and off, the Australian skipper stays behind the line and blocks.
Steven Smith walks in at No.4. A leg gully and a catching mid-wicket fielder in place.

OUT! The decision stays and Usman Khawaja is gone! The decision to keep Jimmy Anderson going has paid off, a wicket has come finally. He continues from around the wicket and angles it in on middle and off, it moves away after hitting the deck and beats the outside edge, catching Khawaja on the back pad. Loud shout and the umpire raises his finger. Usman thinks he might be safe so he reviews. Replays show it's the umpire's call on impact, so the decision will not be overturned. Australia won't lose the review, but Khawaja will have to make the long walk back.
Usman Khawaja has been caught leg before and given out. Looks plumb to the naked eye. He think the away swing will make the ball miss the stumps. So after talking to his partner, he reviews.
Uses the angle well and works it through mid-wicket for a single.
Leaves the ball seeing it's well away from the off stump.
Full wide outside off, no shot offered by the batsman.
Anderson with an extended spell. Joe Root wanting a wicket desperately here, it seems. Wants to exploit the condition to its fullest, so he's using his premier bowler for that.
Stays full, on the stumps, pushed back down the track with the full face of the bat.
Full delivery targeting the off stump, sweetly driven through covers for one.
David Warner offers a firm punch square to point. The length ball was around off, slanting across the batsman.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Short of a length, close to off, Warner is up on his toes as he plays that down.
Shortish in length outside off, Warner opens the face of the bat a bit to punch it through the covers but fails to do so. Gets beaten past the outside edge.
That kicked up suddenly. Landed on a length around off, Khawaja is taken by surprise due to the extra bounce and hence, takes a blow on the gloves as he tries to keep it down.
Marginally ahead of a length well outside off, pushed away to point by opening his body up a bit.
Goes full and it's the inswinger from Jimmy Anderson, Khawaja brings down a straight bat and jams it out. Rather confidently too, I might add.
Rising off the surface as it goes behind to Jonny Bairstow, another left alone.
Similar delivery, but without any kind of movement on it this time. Usman Khawaja leaves it alone.
Comes from around the wicket and serves it outside the line of off stump. Khawaja sees the length ball moving away so lets it be.
Anderson to bowl another over. Hmm...
Another outside off, another leave. Third in a row to end the over.
Chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Good carry for Chris Woakes. Outside off on a length, zipping off the surface a bit, David Warner lets it through.
Cutting back in on middle and leg, on a bit of a back of a length, clipped away through square leg for a run.
Short ball around off, Warner steers this square past point, to the man in the deep for a single.
Overpitched delivery outside off, Warner leans into the shot and drives hard. Connects well, only to find the man at cover.

Drinks break then. Australia have done really well to not lose more than a wicket so far. The ball has been swinging and seaming and doing all sorts of things. Only complaint from England would be that they have been inconsistent. Anderson, for instance, has bowled more short stuff than full while Broad has bowled too wide. The batsmen will feel a bit more confident now that they have negated the new ball but then now comes that period when every batsman is playing for the close.
The ball strikes the batsman very low on the pads. The batsmen have run through for a single. The Umpire signals a leg bye. AUSTRALIA LEAD BY 250.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Played to the point region by the batsman.
On a good length around off, watchfully defended.
Full and slipped down the leg side, losing radar, David lets it go.
Full and outside off, left alone.
The batsman delicately works it fine down the leg side. The batsmen have picked up a couple of runs.
On a good length around middle, Khawaja misses his tuck and is hit on the pads.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Wider outside off, let through again.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
Short and outside off, Khawaja misses out, cutting it straight to cover.
Chris Woakes comes into the attack.
One more leave outside off to end the over. Might be the end of Jimmy for the day.
Landed outside off, let through.
On a length around off, watchfully defended.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Better ball but that is a good leave. The ball is full, pitched around middle but Warner is watching it closely and lets it go away.
Full and wide outside off, plenty of banana swing but too wide to make any impact. Left alone.
FOUR! CLUNK! One of the most authoritative pull shots in this match. Banged in short and Khawaja is ready. Swivels in a flash and pulls it like a rash to see the ball crash into the square leg fence.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Down the leg side, tucked towards square leg.
Around off, watchfully defended.

FOUR! That is lucky again. Full and outside off, Khawaja pushes at it but gets a thick outside edge between third slip and gully to the fence behind. The lead is now 243. The stand moves to 23. Khawaja goes past Warner too, to 13.
On a good length around off, watchfully defended.
Craig Overton into the attack. Was impressive in the first innings.
Outside off again, let through.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
FOUR! Full and down the leg side, plenty of swing, Warner slips but manages to get bat on ball and tickles it to the fine leg fence.
Outside off, left alone.
A length ball on middle and leg, tucked through square leg for a single.

Appeal for a catch but no bat involved. Nice bowling though. The ball is pitched outside leg and is moving away from the southpaw. Khawaja is forced to play at that and the ball goes off something to the keeper. But Anderson does not appeal at all while the slips put in a muted one. The ball had hit the back leg.
Works this through mid-wicket for an easy single.
Outside off, Khawaja feels for it but is squared up and is beaten once again.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Outside off, left alone again.

Full on middle, swings in, Warner is a bit surprised and chips it wide of mid on. Once the ball hits the turf it speeds like a tuxedo and Moeen Ali has to jog harder to get to it. He does manage to do so, but near the ropes, with a slide. Three runs taken.
Full and wide outside off, nice prodigious swing but can be comfortably left alone. And is.
Outside off, fuller in length, the tempting drive on offer but Khawaja resists. It swings back in a long way. But no danger.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Down the leg side, short in length, UK misses his tuck.
Nope. Again the outswinger. Usman is squared up a touch as he pokes at it but the outside edge does not carry to gully.
Landed outside leg, Khawaja feels for it but then the ball moves away to beat the outside edge. Indipper coming?
Wide outside off, left alone.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
Outside off, going away, left alone.

Full and wide outside off, DW reaches out to drive but misses. Poor choice of a shot. Perhaps he went after it seeing the width. Oh wow. Broad thinks there is an edge but Bairstow and Root cannot hear anything. Broad asks, 'No edge?' 'No!' is the answer from Root.
The ball is way outside the off stump, easy leave for the batsman.
Down the leg side, Usman misses out, getting a ball on the pads and not making use of the opportunity. Gets hit on the pads. The ball goes to the leg side and the batsmen take a leg bye.
A length ball down the leg side, Khawaja happily tucks it through square leg. Craig Overton is not the quickest on the park and there is a chance of the third but the batsmen settle for two.
The batsman appears to have been struck on the thigh pad.
Outside off, Warner feels for this one, it is the outswinger and gets beaten again.
Down the leg side, DW misses his flick.
Beautiful bowling. Full and swinging in, but it is too straight. David does miss and is hit on the pads but it was going down leg. So GG, it came on the third ball. Not the fourth. But fair point.
Around middle and off, watchfully defended.

Outside off, prodigious swing, left alone. My colleague GG predicts an inswinger on the fourth ball of this over. We too feel that Anderson is trying to set the batsmen up. Outswingers, Outswingers, outswingers and then boom. Inswinger.

EDGED, FOUR! Countless times we have seen Khawaja getting squared up when the ball is moving around. Countless times we have seen him get runs through that slip cordon. This time too, he does. He is squared up, looking to defend, but the ball seams away and takes the outside edge which goes past third slip to third man!
Full and outside off, swinging away, pushed through the covers for a single.

Yes, that is more like it. Broad gets this right, lands the ball just outside off and then makes it to come back in a long way and then go away at the last moment. DW hops to defend but misses. Broad gives a stare but Warner just smiles.
Waste, waste. The ball is swinging and Broad is bowling it wide outside off. Left alone.
A tad shorter than the previous one, defended from the crease.
Full on middle, pushed straight to mid on.
Outside off, easier to leave, and that is what Usman does.

I think we are seeing one of the most brilliant exhibitions of fast bowling. There is seam and there is swing. Plus there is a plethora of bowlers extracting those. Jimmy pitches this outside leg and then gets it to move away outside off. Play that, if you can. Khawaja cannot, hence is beaten.
Outside off, left alone.
A tad short, around middle, defended watchfully.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Another pearler. The ball is pitched on middle, the length is full which means Khawaja has to bring his bat down to defend but then it bounces and seams away to beat the outside edge.
Too full and straight, clipped through mid-wicket for a single to get off the mark.
Full and tempting to be driven outside off, Usman lets it go.
Another beauty. Full and around off, coming in, then moving away as Khawaja pokes at it.
Outside off, David pushes it through the covers for a single. Gets off the mark.
Outside off, a touch wide, left alone.
Full and outside off, Warner feels for it but misses.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat. A terrific wicket maiden by Jimmy.
Full and outside off, UK feels for it and gets squared up. The ball goes off the outside edge and goes along the ground to gully.
A length ball now, around leg, Usman tries to tuck it away but misses and is hit on the box. Someone appeals from behind for LBW. Seriously.
That is a ripper! Anderson keeps this full and just outside off, Khawaja feels for this but it comes back in and goes past the inside edge and just misses the off pole!
Usman Khawaja walks in at number 3, replacing Bancroft.

OUT! This time the edge goes to hand! Anderson strikes early for England. The perfect outswinger. Pitched outside off, draws the batsman forward and then makes it move away. Bancroft feels for it and gets a thick outside edge. Straight to Bairstow. Just the start England need and the confidence boost Anderson needed. He has been average against the Australians both in England and Australia but this pink ball can change that. If he gets it right, he can run right through that Aussie top order. Australia are effectively 220/1.

Edged, does not carry! This is what extra pace can do. When the Aussies were bowling, whenever there was an edge, 90 percent of those went to hand. However, for Anderson, it is not the case. He bowls this at 133.4 kph, outside off, Bancroft feels for it and nicks it. Bairstow dives to his right but cannot reach it and the ball does not carry anyway.
Outside off, let through.

NOT OUT. Nothing. No sound. No spike. Waste of a review. Full and outside off, Warner looks to flick it to the leg side but misses. No one hears anything but Bairstow keeps on appealing while Broad says he did not hear a thing. Root takes the review and to his dismay, finds nothing.
Is that a nick? Broad says he did not hear anything. Bairstow certainly did. And Root takes the review...
Much, much better. Full and straight, pushed back down the ground.
Finally gets it in line of the stumps and David defends.
One more wide ball, outside off, not played at.
Another widish ball, but not as much as the previous one, left alone.

WIDE! Not as bad as the Steve Harmison blunder in the 2006-07 Ashes but this comes as a good competition. Full and miles outside off, swings out of the pitch and Bairstow has to take it in front of first slip. After all this, Broad is not happy that it is wided. Sad. The lead is now 220.
Stuart Broad to bowl from the other end.

FOUR! Bancroft is away! Not in the most convincing fashion. Outside off, full again, it swings away and induces an outside edge as Bancroft pushes at it. The ball squirts past third slip to the third man fence.
Outside off, left alone.
There is that length, full and just around off, Bancroft just about manages to dig it back to the bowler.
Much better. Gets the length full outside off, CB pushes it off the outer half towards gully.
Slightly quicker than the previous one but too short and too wide outside off. Cameron hops across and keeps his bat inside the line.
A short ball to start, outside off, Bancroft stays away from that line. Straightaway, the difference in pace is seen. 127 kph is the first ball. Starc's first was 140-plus.
